title: CODION: An OWL Ontology for Knowledge-Graph Representation of Disinformation Campaigns and Cognitive Warfare
content: Disinformation, influence operations, and cognitive warfare are increasingly analysed through heterogeneous taxonomies and technical frameworks that address only parts of the wider information environment. This study develops the Cognitive Operations, Disinformation and Influence Ontology (CODION) as a formal knowledge representation model for integrating content, actors, campaigns, targeting, vulnerabilities, effects, evidence, and countermeasures within a common knowledge graph. CODION was derived through structured comparative analysis of relevant analytical frameworks, threat-intelligence models, standards, and prior ontologies, followed by ontology-engineering refinement and OWL 2/RDF formalisation. The resulting five-module architecture separates domain entities, operational structures, consequences and response, and analytical or evidentiary constructs. Key results include an eight-facet Actor architecture, a general TargetingRelation extending beyond audience segments, explicit separation of operational role from measured network position, contextual modelling of vulnerability and topic assessment, a four-stage ImmediateEffect–Outcome–Impact–Harm chain, and an Assertion/Evidence pattern for contested or probabilistic information. Competency-oriented SPARQL scenarios demonstrate query support for coordination, institutional targeting, network analysis, causal pathways, topic exploitability, and audience progression. CODION provides a semantic and interoperable foundation for modelling disinformation and counterdisinformation ecosystems and for integrating heterogeneous analytical outputs in threat-intelligence and decision-support environments.
